  COVID-19 PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT REGARDING MEETINGS OF
  THE INGLEWOOD CITY COUNCIL AND OTHER CITY LEGISLATIVE BODIES

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood City Council and other City legislative bodies will be conducted
pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e), which allows the City to use teleconferencing for
members of the public to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in option.

CALL-IN OPTION

  1. Members of the public who wish to attend a public meeting and address the City Council or other
  legislative body during a public meeting must use the call-in option noted below:

  l  Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments telephonically by dialing:
  l Dial-in for Closed Session: 1-669-900-6833 Meeting ID: 825 5030 7638 Passcode: 024788
  l Dial-in for Open Session: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694, using the specific
  access codes detailed below for the respective City Council Dates:

  l  June 28, 2022 – Access Code: 6178183# wait 3 seconds and press # again

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting the meeting to the public using the call-in
option, or in the event of a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from offering public
comments using the call-in option, the City Council and other legislative body shall take no further action on items
appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

appearing on the meeting agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS

The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to submit comments and/or to observe a
public meeting. The following alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience only and
the disruption in service to any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body from
taking further action on an agenda item. In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below members of
the public should use the call-in option above.

2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or
subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00
a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact
the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
  details.
  l Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

4. Public attendance at Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) to view
meeting and make public comments via audio/video.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any

the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard,

aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

  22-101 ADOPTED – TO ESTABLISH SHORT TERM RENTAL REGISTRATION

  2
 June 28, 2022

  PERMIT FEES TO BE INCLUDED IN THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE. The
  City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider
  establishing short term rental regulations and fees by taking the following actions:

  1.  Introduce an ordinance amending Inglewood Municipal Code Chapters 8
  (Businesses, Trades, and Professions) and 12 (Planning and Zoning), including
  Zoning Code Amendment 2018-001 (ZCA-2018-01) to establish Short Term
  Rental Regulations; and
  2.  Adopt a resolution to establish Short Term Rental Registration Permit Fees to
  be  included in the Master Fee Schedule, notice had been given in the time, form,
  and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communication were received
  and distributed to the Mayor and Council Members.

  Artie Fields, City Manager presented the Staff Report dated June 28, 2022.

  Yakema Decatur, Deputy to the City Manager/Housing Protection Deputy Director,
  presented an oral report on the City of Inglewood's Short Term Rental (STR) Regulations.
  She defined an STR and how STRs are primarily booked. She also stated that
  approximately 500 STRs in the City of Inglewood account for over 800 listings. As of
  June 15, 2022, 326 warning notices were mailed to those identified as operating an
  unpermitted STR. Ms. Decatur reviewed the purpose and stated the department intended
  to create an enforcement structure to maintain the residential neighborhood's tranquility,
  character, and integrity. At the same time, long-term Inglewood residents would be
  allowed to supplement their household income by benefiting from the city's desirability as
  a sports entertainment destination center. She also outlined the proposed policies for STRs
  hosted and unhosted, and vacation rental qualifications.

  Council Member Morales inquired about the vacation rental, and asked does it apply to the
  whole house that the host is residing in?

  Ms. Decatur informed Council Member Morales that it does.

  Council Member Morales also inquired if the person must have lived in residence, been an
  Inglewood resident for ten years, and owned a separate home for a year.

  Ms. Decatur stated and owned their primary residence for five years.

  Council Member Morales asked if a person has owned a home for less than five years, but
  they’re renting it from a duplex or a room in their home, are they okay.

  Ms. Decatur stated yes, they are. She also stated she believed the proposal for duplexes,
  triplexes, and fourplexes kept the intention of the City Council when considering the
  mom-and-pop owners. It allowed them to make an additional income, especially with the
  impacts of the pandemic and not receiving rent.

  Mayor Butts stated that the City gives people who own smaller apartment buildings the
  same opportunity as people who own single-family residences.

  Ms. Decatur reiterated that duplexes, triplexes, and fourplexes owners’ must reside on the
  property and have at least one vacant unity to operate as a vacation rental.

  Mayor Butts commented that an owner couldn’t be an LLC or live in another city and
  operate an STR as a business. He also stated the City is trying as best as possible to
  preserve housing access for people who want to reside in Inglewood, enabling those who
  live in the city to conduct the STRs. Finally, he stated that the City does not wish for
  companies to buy properties, making them STRs and eroding the housing stock. The
  Mayor asked Yakema if he was correct.

  Ms. Decatur stated the Mayor was correct with his comment. She also stated that vacation
  rentals are limited to 90 days per calendar year. If an owner uses an STR platform, they
  must pay the City the Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) of 15.5%. Additionally, she added
  that the onus would be on the owner to ensure it was done.

  3
 June 28, 2022

  Ms. Decatur reviewed the Registration Requirements and stated that every host that
  desired to obtain an STR permit must file an application with the city of Inglewood. They
  must also remit the annual registration fee, adhere to the rules and regulations set forth in
  the City of Inglewood's STR Ordinance, renew annually, and maintain an active STR
  permit and residential rental business tax certificate. Additionally, Ms. Decatur reviewed
  the Regulations and Prohibitions. She stated accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and
  properties with five or more units on a parcel are not eligible to operate as an STR. She
  also stated that there are no party houses, and STRs remain subject to restrictions and
  limitations pursuant to the Homeowners Association's covenants, conditions, and
  restrictions. She further stated that STRs operating in permit parking districts would only
  be allowed one parking permit per booking for off-street parking.

  Mayor Butts commented and clarified the term “party houses,” stating the term covers
  being rented out for an event.

  Ms. Decatur reiterated that an owner of properties that have two or more units on a parcel
  must and are required to register with the Housing Protection Department. All registration
  fees and penalties must be paid before issuing an STR application. She discussed the
  hosting platforms and host responsibilities. She stated that STR hosts and platforms, such
  as Air BNB, VRBO, etc., are prohibited from advertising without a valid STR permit. In
  addition, they must remove any listings for STR from its platform upon notification by the
  City of the violation. She also stated that they are responsible for collecting and remitting
  TOT and comply with all City TOT requirements. Ms. Decatur further emphasized that
  host platforms must disclose each short-term or vacation rental listing in the city monthly,
  along with the names of the person responsible for each listing, the address of each such
  listing, the length of stay for each such listing, and the price paid for each stay.. She
  further stated that the host must provide a code of conduct to all guests that include
  relevant information addressing behavior, safety, and security.

  Ms. Decatur outlined the enforcement and stated that any action by an STR host or owner
  that is an infraction is punishable pursuant to Government Code 36900. She also stated
  that the City may issue and serve administrative subpoenas as necessary to obtain specific
  information regarding STR or vacation rental listings located in the city. Additionally, Ms.
  Decatur stated any STR host who violates any provisions set forth in the STR Ordinance
  may be subject to administrative fines and penalties. Ms. Decatur thanked Sharon Kioke,

  reviewed the compiled fee table and stated the first table consisted of the different
  departments that would help process the permit applications; the second table estimated
  the money required to administer the program. The third table shows the total cost based
  on the number of STRs. She further stated that for 500 STRs, the total fee would be

  be $659.15. She also stated that she believed it was proposed that the fees be reduced in

  reducing the fees to $500 for hosted STRs and $600 for unhosted STRs.

  STRs. Additionally, he added that STRs weren’t the reason for rent increases and felt it
  was due to gentrification, such as the building of SoFi, and the Forum. Finally, he
  proposed that the Council look into developing a policy that owners of properties in
  Inglewood who have long-term renters on the property would find beneficial.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts thanked Sharon Kioke,
  Assistant Finance Director, and Captain Marie DiBernardo for staying the duration of the
  City Council Meeting, and adjourned the meeting at the hour of 5:40 p.m.
